question: Part-IV of the Constitution of India states about which of the following?
solution: The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Part-IV of the Constitution of India** (Articles **36 to 51**) contains the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**. • The Directive Principles aim to establish **social and economic democracy** and serve as guidelines to the **state** for formulating policies and laws to achieve a just society. • These principles are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country. • The concept of DPSP is borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**, which in turn derived it from the **Spanish Constitution**. • The DPSPs include provisions related to **social justice, economic welfare, foreign policy**, and **legal and administrative matters**.
